prompt:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (20 frames); start pose (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (12 frames); animation 7 (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (12 frames); animation 8 (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (20 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 20 to 116 pixels tall and from 12 to 92 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig115_03/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


TARGETED SINGLE-SPRITE RETURN, overrides all generic atlas/full-character descriptions above. Only ONE isolated thin bent BLUE FABRIC CONTOUR fragment is requested, costume115_1882. Image1 is its original pixel geometry, enlarged 48x solely to make the tiny five-pixel-high original readable. Image2 is the approved Sam master for colors and smooth cartoon outline. Image3 is an own, previously self-checked neighboring fragment group for stroke consistency, not an external approval. Original dimensions: 21 pixels wide and 5 high. Keep this EXACT low arch silhouette and enclosed thickness ratio, with the LEFT part almost horizontal and gently rising toward a small raised central ridge, then a LONG near-horizontal middle and a small right end bending down. Preserve ALL the blue region between top and bottom edges; do not turn the center into a thin line, add a big triangular peak, or make a steep symmetric rainbow arch. Keep its shallow wavy lower contour and narrow tapered left tip. The first reference decides all geometry. Paint one smooth non-pixelated, clean dark outlined cobalt/navy blue strip at the same place and size as image1. No luminous rim, pixel steps, extra shadow, glow, texture, labels, neighboring objects, person, complete tie or shirt. Gray is reference padding ONLY. Output one 1536x1024 PNG with real transparent background, softly antialiased own contours, and just that one reference sprite. The final whole asset will be placed at exact original 4x size separately.
